questions.question: Given below is an inequality, which of the following condition is TRUE? If P ≤ Q ≥ R; E ≥ Q; L < Q = D
questions.questionHtml:
Given below is an inequality, which of the following condition is TRUE?

If P ≤ Q ≥ R; E ≥ Q; L < Q = D
questions.solution:
Given inequality is: P ≤ Q ≥ R; E ≥ Q; L < Q = D

1. L < P → P ≤ Q, L < Q, data is not sufficient to determine the relation → False

2. E ≥ R → E ≥ Q ≥ R, E ≥ R → True.

3. E < D → E ≥ Q, L < Q = D, E ≥ D → False.

4. Q < R → Q ≥ R → False.

Hence, E ≥ R, is the correct inequality.

questions.question: Directions: In the following question assuming the given statements to be true, find which of the given conclusions is definitely true. Statement: G < J ≤ V; F ≥ I = G; N ≥ H > F
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In the following question assuming the given statements to be true, find which of the given conclusions is definitely true.

Statement:

G < J ≤ V; F ≥ I = G; N ≥ H > F
questions.solution:
Given:

G < J ≤ V; F ≥ I = G; N ≥ H > F

On Combining:

N ≥ H > F ≥ I = G < J ≤ V

Conclusions:

1. G > H → False (as G = I ≤ F < H; therefore G < H)

2. N ≤ I → False (as N ≥ H > F ≥ I; therefore N > I)

3. I < V → True (as I = G < J ≤ V)

4. N < F → False (as N ≥ H > F; therefore N > F)

Hence, “I < V” is definitely true among the given options.

questions.question: While traveling by bus, a man spent Rs. 60 more than 10 times the fare he paid for an auto rickshaw. The total amount spent by him is 13 times the fare he paid for an auto rickshaw. What total amount of money was spent on Bus as well as Auto rickshaw by the man?
questions.questionHtml: While traveling by bus, a man spent Rs. 60 more than 10 times the fare he paid for an auto rickshaw. The total amount spent by him is 13 times the fare he paid for an auto rickshaw. What total amount of money was spent on Bus as well as Auto rickshaw by the man?
questions.solution:
Let, Man spend fare for auto rickshaw = a ------(i)

Then, Man spend fare for Bus = 10a + 60 Rs ------(ii)

Total amount spent by him = 13a ------(iii)

According to question,

Eq (i) + Eq (ii) = Eq(iii)

a + 10a + 60 = 13a

2a = 60

a = 30

Man spend fare for auto rickshaw = 30 Rs

Man spend fare for Bus = 300 + 60 = 360 Rs

Total amount of money was spent on Bus as well as Auto rickshaw by the man = 360 + 30

= 390 Rs

Hence, 390 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Two buses start from the opposite points of the main road, 150 km apart. The first bus runs for 25 km and takes a right turn and then runs for 15 km. It then turns left and runs for another 25 km and takes the direction back to reach the main road. In the meantime, due to a minor breakdown, the other bus has run only 35 km along the main road. What would be the distance between the two buses at this point?
questions.questionHtml: Two buses start from the opposite points of the main road, 150 km apart. The first bus runs for 25 km and takes a right turn and then runs for 15 km. It then turns left and runs for another 25 km and takes the direction back to reach the main road. In the meantime, due to a minor breakdown, the other bus has run only 35 km along the main road. What would be the distance between the two buses at this point?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance between starting points = 150 km.

Journey of first bus = 25 km, then takes a right turn and then runs for 15 km, then turns left and runs for another 25 km and takes the direction back to reach the main road.

Journey of second bus = 35 km along the main road

Calculations:

Let first bus started from point X.

After running for 25 km, it reaches point A.

⇒ Then took a right turn and then runs for 15 km.

⇒ After reaching point B, turns left and runs parallel to main road for another 25 km.

⇒ After reaching point C, takes the left turn and reached the main road at point D.

Total distance covered by the first bus along main road = 25 + 25 = 50 km 

Let second bus started from point Y.

⇒ Due to a minor breakdown, the second bus has run only 35 km along the main road and reached point E..

Total distance covered by the second bus along main road = 35 km

Distance between both the buses = 150 - (50 + 35)

⇒ 150 - 85

⇒ 65 km

∴ The distance between the two buses at the end is 65 km.

questions.question: The average age of 17 persons is 39 years. If the average age of the first 9 persons is 35 years, and the average age of the last 9 persons is 44 years, what is the age of the 9 th person?
questions.questionHtml: The average age of 17 persons is 39 years. If the average age of the first 9 persons is 35 years, and the average age of the last 9 persons is 44 years, what is the age of the 9<sup>th</sup> person?
questions.solution:
We know that

Average age = Total age of all persons ÷ total persons

So,

Total age of all persons = Average age × total persons

Given:

1) Average age of 17 persons is 39 years.

Total age of all persons = Average age × total persons

= 39 × 17

= 663

2) Average age of the first 9 persons is 35 years.

Total age of the first 9 persons = Average age × total persons

= 35 × 9

= 315

3) Average age of the last 9 persons is 44 years.

Total age of the last 9 persons = Average age × total persons

= 44 × 9

= 396

So,

The age of the 9th person = Total age of the first 9 persons + Total age of the last 9 persons - Total age of all persons  

= 315 + 396 – 663

= 711 – 663

= 48

Hence, the age of the 9th person is ‘48’.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (50 ÷ 3) × 15 + 25 − 10 = 25
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

(50 ÷ 3) × 15 + 25 − 10 = 25
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

In this question, two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct.

Given: (50 ÷ 3) × 15 + 25 − 10 = 25

Option 1) ÷ and -

After interchanging the two signs we get the;

⇒ (50 - 3) × 15 + 25 ÷ 10 = 25

⇒ 47 × 15 + 25 ÷ 10 = 25

⇒ 47 × 15 + 2.5 = 25

⇒ 705 + 2.5 = 25

⇒ 707.5 ≠ 25

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) + and × 

After interchanging the two signs we get the;

⇒ (50 ÷ 3) + 15 × 25 − 10 = 25

⇒ 16.66 + 15 × 25 - 10 = 25

⇒ 16.66 + 375 - 10 = 25

⇒ 391.66 - 10 = 25

⇒ 381.66 ≠ 25

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) ÷ and × 

After interchanging the two signs we get the;

⇒ (50 × 3) ÷ 15 + 25 − 10 = 25

⇒ 150 ÷ 15 + 25 - 10 = 25

⇒ 10 + 25 - 10 = 25

⇒ 35 - 10 = 25

⇒ 25 = 25

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) + and − 

After interchanging the two signs we get the;

⇒ (50 ÷ 3) × 15 - 25 + 10 = 25

⇒ 16.66 * 15 - 25 + 10 = 25

​⇒ 249.9 - 25 + 10 = 25

​⇒ 259.9 - 25 = 25

​⇒ 234.9 ≠ 25

​⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,

A + B means 'A is the mother of B',

A - B means 'A is the brother of B',

A × B means 'A is the wife of B',

A ÷ B means 'A is the father of B'.

questions.solution:
Family Chart:

Decoding the Symbols:

Symbol + - × ÷
Meaning Mother Brother Wife Father

 

Given: M + N ÷ O × P - Q

It means: M is the Mother of N, N is the Father of O, O is the Wife of P, P is the Brother of Q.

So, M is the 'Wife's Father's Mother' of P.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: Four number-pairs are given, out of which three are alike in some way or the other, and one is different. Select the odd number-pair.
questions.questionHtml: Four number-pairs are given, out of which three are alike in some way or the other, and one is different. Select the odd number-pair.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: 1st number = (2nd number ÷ 2) × 3

Checking all the options one by one:

1) 112 : 70 → (70 ÷ 2) × 3 = 35 × 3 = 105 ≠ 1st number

2) 39 : 26 → (26 ÷ 2) × 3 = 13 × 3 = 39 = 1st Number

3) 63 : 42 → (42 ÷ 2) × 3 = 21 × 3 = 63 = 1st Number

4) 30 : 20 → (20 ÷ 2) × 3 = 10 × 3 = 30 = 1st Number

Hence, the correct answer is "112 : 70".

questions.question: In the question below is given a statement followed by some courses of action. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the suggested course of action logically follow(s) for pursuing. Statement : While you are working at a Multinational company in a Metropolitan city, you notice your colleague having acute chest pain and you realize that it could be a Heart Attack.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question below is given a statement followed by some courses of action. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the suggested course of action logically follow(s) for pursuing.

Statement: While you are working at a Multinational company in a Metropolitan city, you notice your colleague having acute chest pain and you realize that it could be a Heart Attack.

options.text: Call Ambulance and wait till it arrives.
options.html: Call Ambulance and wait till it arrives.

options.text: Take him to the hospital as soon as possible in your private vehicle.
options.html: Take him to the hospital as soon as possible in your private vehicle.

options.text: Ask your other colleagues to help him as you have a major assignment to be submitted by the end of the day.
options.html: Ask your other colleagues to help him as you have a major assignment to be submitted by the end of the day.

options.text: Ask your Boss to take the responsibility of taking him to the hospital.
options.html: Ask your Boss to take the responsibility of taking him to the hospital.

questions.solution:
The Logic here is as follows: 

  • The correct answer is Option 2: Take him to the hospital as soon as possible

in your private vehicle.

 

Course of Action Correction Reasoning
Call Ambulance and wait till it arrives. Incorrect During a Heart Attack, the first 30mins are very crucial. Hence, waiting for the Ambulance to arrive can actually make the condition worst.
Take him to the hospital as soon as possible in your private vehicle. Correct This is correct because, taking the person to the hospital as soon as possible during the Heart Attack can actually save his life, as the first 30mins are very important.
Ask your other colleagues to help him as you have a major assignment to be submitted by the end of the day. Incorrect This would be Incorrect because doing this would be very Selfish, as you think your work is more important than the life of a person.
Ask your Boss to take the responsibility of taking him to the hospital. Incorrect This would be Incorrect because you have no power to give order to your Boss.

 

  • Qualities Projected in this situation:  (Sens of responsibility,

Effective intelligence, and speed of decision).

Key Points

  • Checklist for attempting Course of Action questions:
  1. Read the question and options carefully.
  2. Look for options that are realistic, optimistic, and reflect officer-like qualities.
  3. Do not skip any situation.
  4. Relegate the negative sentences and choose the most logical option among the remaining ones. As time is an important factor, hence your thinking ability should be swift.
  5. React quickly and be logical.

A and B are living adjacent to each other. There is two floor gap between E and D who is living on the floor number which is a multiple of two. C is living above A and E. Who among the following lives on the second floor.
